label: Fiedler's July 4 concerts begin
detail: Arthur Fiedler's July 4 Esplanade concerts date to 1929, before the Hatch Shell existed.

label: Cavalcade of Jazz begins
detail: An annual large-scale jazz event at Wrigley Field, Los Angeles, predating Newport.

label: First Newport Jazz Festival
detail: Tickets were $3 to $5; Billie Holiday and Dizzy Gillespie played opening night.

label: First Newport Folk Festival
detail: Founded at Freebody Park by George Wein, Albert Grossman, Pete Seeger, Theodore Bikel and Oscar Brand.

label: Newport Jazz riot
detail: Crowds shut out of sold-out shows clashed with police; about 200 arrests reported and the National Guard called.

label: Dylan plays electric at Newport Folk
detail: First public performance of Like a Rolling Stone; accounts of the crowd's reaction differ.

label: Dylan goes electric at Newport Folk
detail: His first plugged-in professional set; some booed, and accounts of who and why are still contested.

label: Monterey Pop
detail: Artists play for charity; first major US appearances for the Jimi Hendrix Experience and the Who.

label: Woodstock
detail: Planned for about 50,000; an estimated 460,000 to 500,000 attend.

label: Altamont
detail: UPI reports a crowd of upwards of 300,000 and four deaths.

label: Glastonbury founded
detail: Michael Eavis founds Glastonbury.

label: Isle of Wight Festival
detail: Guinness estimate of 600,000 to 700,000; declared free when profit became impossible.

label: First Glastonbury
detail: £1 with free milk from the farm; 1,500 people attended.

label: Fence crash halts Newport Jazz
detail: More than 12,000 people broke through the fence during Dionne Warwick's set.

label: Roskilde begins as the Sound Festival
detail: 10,000 to 13,000 people, 30 Danish kroner a ticket.

label: First Roskilde
detail: Held as the Sound Festival; 10,000 to 13,000 attend at 30 kroner.

label: Roskilde begins donating its surplus
detail: 457 million DKK donated since, per 2026 official figures.

label: First Pops Fireworks Spectacular
detail: About 75,000 heard the 1812 Overture with cannons and fireworks; David Mugar paid about $10,000.

label: Rock Werchter debuts
detail: About 650 people attended the first edition.

label: Newport Jazz returns to Fort Adams
detail: Back in Newport as a daytime-only, alcohol-free event on three stages.

label: Newport Folk revived
detail: Brought back at Fort Adams State Park after dormancy since 1969.

label: Glastonbury's first fallow year
detail: A year off to give the land, locals and organizers a break.

label: First Lollapalooza tour
detail: Opens at Compton Terrace, Arizona; 20 dates that summer.

label: UK Pop Code published
detail: Noise Council code sets music noise targets at nearby homes.

label: Pulp replace The Stone Roses at Glastonbury
detail: An early example of a headliner swap after the bill was set (vendor summary).

label: First Fuji Rock
detail: A typhoon hit day one and day two was canceled.

label: Woodstock '99 water prices
detail: Water was reportedly sold at $4 rising to $12 (secondary source).

label: Woodstock '99 opens in Rome, New York
detail: Heat over 100 F on the tarmac, $4 water, three deaths (HISTORY).

label: Attitude is Everything founded
detail: The UK charity launched its Charter of Best Practice for live music access.

label: Exit founded in Novi Sad
detail: Started by student activists in Serbia.

label: Roskilde crowd crush
detail: Nine young men die at the Orange Stage during Pearl Jam's set.

label: Splendour in the Grass begins
detail: Australia's flagship festival, later canceled in 2024 and 2025.

label: Denmark publishes a national concert safety guide
detail: Followed the Roskilde 2000 disaster.

label: Coachella's descending-font-size poster begins
detail: Coachella has kept a ranked, size-by-status poster format since 2003, per Wallpaper*.

label: Disabled Stewards Festivals Programme
detail: Attitude is Everything began placing disabled volunteers in steward roles.

label: First Tomorrowland
detail: About 10,000 people at De Schorre, Boom.

label: Lollapalooza's Grant Park deal
detail: A 10-year Grant Park deal through 2018 bars rival multi-day festivals in the park.

label: Illinois investigates radius clauses
detail: Attorney General Lisa Madigan opens an antitrust investigation into Lollapalooza's radius clause.

label: Love Parade disaster, Duisburg
detail: 21 dead and 652 injured at a crush on the main ramp (per Wikipedia).

label: Newport Festivals Foundation
detail: George Wein set up the nonprofit that has run both Newport festivals since.

label: Tomorrowland's aftermovie
detail: The half-hour recap passed 70 million views by 2015 and spread the aftermovie format.

label: Indiana State Fair stage collapse
detail: Seven die when a temporary stage roof fails in wind below its code minimum.

label: Pukkelpop storm
detail: Five die; the Belgian festival is canceled the next day.

label: Events Industry Forum takes over the Purple Guide
detail: Publication passes from the Health and Safety Executive.

label: Lollapalooza sells out before its lineup
detail: Three-day passes sold out in under three hours with no lineup announced, which organizers called a festival first.

label: Boston Calling debuts
detail: First edition at City Hall Plaza over Memorial Day weekend, created by Brian Appel and Mike Snow.

label: Live Nation partners with Insomniac
detail: A 'creative partnership' with EDC's producer; a stake of roughly $50 million was reported.

label: Live Nation buys into C3 Presents
detail: A reported 51% of Lollapalooza's producer for a reported $125 million.

label: Cells on wheels at Coachella
detail: AT&T began deploying COWs at Coachella; data hit about 24 TB that year.

label: Nyege Nyege launches in Jinja, Uganda
detail: About 20,000 attended by 2023.

label: The Show Must Go On report and Vision: 2025 pledge
detail: UK festivals asked to cut emissions 50% by 2025.

label: Utrecht earplug trial
detail: 12% of festivalgoers with earplugs vs 40% without had tinnitus or temporary hearing loss.

label: 29.2 TB at Coachella
detail: AT&T reported 29.2 TB of cellular data over Coachella's two weekends.

label: SFX files for bankruptcy
detail: The dance music roll-up files Chapter 11 and later re-emerges as LiveStyle.

label: MSG buys into Boston Calling
detail: The Madison Square Garden Company buys a controlling interest; Brian Appel stays CEO.

label: Boston Calling moves to Allston
detail: Sound bleed across the Charles brings complaints from Cambridge.

label: Coachella grosses $114.6 million
detail: Billboard reports the two-weekend gross, the last public Coachella figure.

label: Boston Calling security steps up after Manchester
detail: Bag checks, bomb techs and dogs at its first Allston edition.

label: AEG takes full ownership of Firefly
detail: AEG Presents buys out Red Frog Events' remaining shares.

label: Billy McFarland sentenced
detail: The Fyre Festival founder gets six years in federal prison.

label: Glastonbury bans plastic bottle sales
detail: First full single-use plastic bottle sales ban; more than 99% of tents reported taken home.

label: Roskilde introduces reusable cups
detail: About 2 million cups now used per festival.

label: The IFF billing debate
detail: At the International Festival Forum in London, Roskilde described its 100/90/70/50/40% font tiers and others argued against A-Z billing.

label: Glastonbury drops single-use plastic bottles
detail: No plastic drinks bottles sold at the 2019 festival after over 1 million sold in 2017.

label: Woodstock 50 financier pulls out
detail: Dentsu Aegis withdraws more than $18 million; the festival never happens.

label: AIF launches Take Your Tent Home
detail: Campaign against an estimated 250,000 abandoned tents a year.

label: Town of Vernon rejects Woodstock 50 appeal
detail: Planning board vote is unanimous.

label: Electric Forest's loyalty ladder
detail: Electric Forest announced 2020 presale tiers rewarding up to six years of attendance.

label: Ninth Circuit revives Soul'd Out case
detail: An appeals panel reverses the dismissal of the Coachella radius clause lawsuit.

label: Astroworld crowd crush
detail: Ten people die at the Houston festival.

label: Astroworld crowd crush, Houston
detail: Ten die of compression asphyxiation during Travis Scott's set.

label: Live Events Access Charter
detail: Attitude is Everything introduced its updated access charter.

label: Glastonbury tents: 99% home
detail: About 99% of tents taken home from roughly 210,000 attendees, per the organizer.

label: Texas Task Force on Concert Safety report
detail: Recommends unified command, codes of conduct and stricter permit enforcement.

label: Boston Calling goes cashless
detail: Wristbands became both ticket and payment, WBUR reported.

label: Coachella's late reveal delays Boston Calling
detail: Boston Calling, Bonnaroo and Sonic Temple had planned a January 10 announcement and had to wait.

label: Glastonbury runs all generators on HVO
detail: Fuel made from used cooking oil, with a claimed CO2 cut of up to 90%.

label: Houston police release Astroworld report
detail: 1,266 pages; a grand jury had declined to indict.

label: A Greener Future travel study
detail: Audience travel averages 41% of festival emissions, range 18% to 76%.

label: Electric Zoo day one canceled
detail: Missing NYC Parks permits; Sunday gate rush after reported overselling.

label: The Loop gets first Home Office festival drug checking licence
detail: Returns to Parklife after being blocked in 2023.

label: Record UK festival losses
detail: AIF counts a record 78 UK festivals canceled, postponed or closed.

label: Boston Calling Sunday crowding
detail: Mayor Wu says EMS transfers far exceeded other days.

label: KKR buys Superstruct
detail: Providence Equity announces the sale; a reported $1.4 billion.

label: Third straight 99% at Glastonbury
detail: Emily Eavis said 99% of all tents had been taken home.

label: UK CMA investigates the Oasis on-sale
detail: The regulator opened an investigation into Ticketmaster's use of dynamic pricing in the August 31, 2024 sale.

label: Glastonbury shares pass to Emily Eavis
detail: Michael Eavis transfers his shares and stays a director.

label: Tomorrowland's 18-minute presale
detail: 200,000 Belgian presale tickets sold in 18 minutes, a record.

label: Newport Folk sells out with no lineup
detail: The 2025 festival sold out in under a minute without naming a single performer (reported).

label: Fake Ultra wristbands arrest
detail: A man was reported arrested for allegedly selling two fake Ultra wristbands for $1,200.

label: High Court quashes Brockwell Park certificate
detail: Residents win case against Lambeth Council over the 28-day rule.

label: US all-in ticket pricing rule
detail: The FTC rule requiring total prices with mandatory fees took effect.

label: Bonnaroo canceled by storms
detail: Fields evacuated after flooding and a forecast of more heavy rain.

label: Boston Calling pauses for 2026
detail: Organizers announced no 2026 festival and a return June 4-6, 2027.

label: Exit's last edition in Serbia ends
detail: Organizers cited financial and political pressure.

label: Fire destroys Tomorrowland's main stage
detail: No injuries; the festival went ahead on both weekends.

label: Queensland bans pill testing
detail: Follows April 2025 closure of the two CheQpoint sites.

label: Newport Festivals Accessibility Program
detail: Register after buying on DICE; companion wristband and on-site Accessibility Hub.

label: Glastonbury fallow year
detail: The next festival is set for June 23-27, 2027.

label: Transport and Environment questions HVO
detail: Says best-case HVO only halves CO2 vs diesel.

label: Newport Folk sells out blind
detail: 2026 tickets appeared to sell out within seconds on DICE before any lineup was announced.

label: Glastonbury 2027 standard tickets on sale
detail: Tickets requiring photo registration and a £100 deposit went on sale and later showed as sold out.
